knownCoverageGaps: Gateway restart performance is deferred to #105; representative and stress require the other four recovery fault classes. The real Gateway restart directory-recovery correctness test remains in the default Browser suite.
A deliberately slow raw WebSocket client and concurrent history/command fairness are not yet benchmarked.

Stress concurrency reports actual arrival rate, and the sustained-load scenario declares a fixed 60 second window at 125 delta/s per Session across 8 Sessions, so the achieved aggregate rate is bounded at half the declared schedule and reported diagnostically above that. An independently certified uninterrupted 1,000 aggregate delta/s arrival ceiling remains unmeasured.
Generic typed content-root references are covered by the default Browser gate but are not benchmarked as a separate performance scenario; this suite measures production attachment refs.
Browser-triggered history cancellation and post-cancel process/heap release are not yet measured; the server cancellation contract is covered separately.
The deterministic Pi fixture proves repeatable protocol behavior, not real-provider or heterogeneous reference-host performance.
Multiple Browser clients sharing the same Gateway and adversarial socket backpressure remain outside Phase 1.

Full mounting of a 5,000-Turn mixed history costs approximately 122 s per cycle, above the 120 s per-cycle execution safety cap, so that cell is not measurable as declared. The bounded 5,000-Turn cell and the 1,000-Turn full-mount cell remain the measured anchors of the mounting cost curve.

Recovery faults are injected during active text streaming only. Fault injection during thinking, tool execution, queued input, and blocking Extension UI is not implemented, and the retry-count and terminal-degraded-state metrics are absent from trial records.

Gateway and Browser peak memory, snapshot build count, and admission latency are not recorded. Per-Session progress delay and post-cancel process/heap release remain unmeasured; starvation prevention is only covered as the concurrency scenario's background-progress checkpoints, which assert that every Session keeps ingesting while another is foreground rather than measuring a delay distribution.
